title: Explain Your Book Choice

source.rights: 原创 AI 辅助虚构教学材料；尚待独立教学与发音审核。

instructions: Prepare briefly and record your own response of 120–160 words. The sample is shorter than the 90–120 second target. Add relevant details and allow natural pauses while staying within 120–160 words.
prompt: Speak for about 90–120 seconds, using 120–160 words. Describe a fictional book you would choose for a reading group, explain its genre and one character or idea, and tell a new member when to register and how to keep the room comfortable. Use at least six lesson words.
reference: For our fictional reading group, I would choose a paperback mystery from the library. The main character is a detective who finds a note on a train. The plot is not too difficult, and the story has some humour as well as an adventure. I would use the catalogue to locate the right edition, then ask whether my membership is still active. A new reader should register by Monday, because the meeting is on Wednesday. The book is due the following week, but we can ask the desk if we need more time. During the meeting, everyone can read a short part and explain why it is interesting. We should keep the noise low and whisper while someone is reading. I would also bring a translation of a classic to show the group another possible genre.
